correctness.rationale: The four-de-Bruijn-state predecessor relation for Rule 110 has label matrices R_0=0x8101 and R_1=0x42c2, verified independently by enumerating all eight local neighborhoods. A periodic output w∞ has a bi-infinite predecessor iff Boolean relation R_w has a directed cycle of length ≤4; any such cycle may realize an antecedent period multiple of |w|, so the proof avoids a same-period antecedent assumption. Independent Boolean-relation closure from identity has exactly 75 reachable states. With transfer T, acceptance vector v is killed coordinatewise by T⁹−4T⁸+6T⁷−5T⁶+T⁵+4T⁴−4T³+2T²−I; the independent implementation confirmed all 75 exact integer coordinates. The first ten counts and rational generating-function logarithmic-derivative identity then certify ζ for every n, not merely finitely many n. Period two is excluded by the two failed alternating words. The relations R_1^kR_0 have a directed cycle for k≥2 and R_1 powers stabilize at k=5, so 1^(n−1)0 gives a primitive witness for every n≥3. Finite ring checks are only corroborative.
